answer: An attacker who floods the jury with fake votes also floods itself with the cost of its own dishonest votes, because every vote is penalized when it backs a bad answer. This works because the originality bar tightens as more low-quality answers appear, raising the per-alias cost of a coordinated fake campaign. The effect is that voting power tracks real contribution, so a flood of accounts cannot outvote a smaller set of genuinely established participants. Consider a umber as the anchor of the cost.
